concept: MongoDB PHP library and Laravel MongoDB, the Ruby driver and Mongoid, and the Scala driver
summary: Source-anchored research for MongoDB PHP library and Laravel MongoDB, the Ruby driver and Mongoid, and the Scala driver. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The Composer package mongodb/mongodb is a high-level PHP library layered over the mongodb extension. It provides client, database, and collection abstractions plus CRUD and common-command helpers. (high confidence)
The upgrade guide states that library and extension patch versions are not synchronized and provides separate update commands for each component. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
A custom `Codec` implements `encode()`, `decode()`, and `getEncoderClass()`; the codec registry must contain a codec for the Scala type being encoded or decoded. (low confidence)
Single-document writes are atomic. Use a multi-document transaction when several document writes must be applied or discarded together. (high confidence)

Referenced associations are not autosaved by default when saving their parent; enable `autosave` when required. Embedded documents are saved within the parent, and nested-attributes associations automatically gain autosave behavior. (low confidence)
Mongoid coerces query values to a declared field’s type when constructing a query. Wrap a value in `Mongoid::RawValue` to bypass this coercion. (low confidence)
A collection query can filter embedded fields using dot notation, but it returns top-level model instances even when every condition references embedded fields. (high confidence)

When Composer reports that the mongodb extension is missing despite it appearing in another PHP environment, check which PHP binary Composer uses and which configuration the CLI and web runtime load. (high confidence)

When an installed extension is unavailable at runtime, check the PHP runtime and its configuration: multiple PHP versions have separate extension-install commands, and CLI and web environments can load different php.ini files. (high confidence)

Coinbase reported in June 2020 that its Ruby processes each maintained a MongoDB pool shared by that process’s threads, and that blue-green deployment overlap increased the database connection count. This is a historical production example of connection multiplication across processes and deployment replicas. (low confidence)
Construct a Mongo::Client with a MongoDB connection URI; most applications can reuse a single client across multiple requests because it owns connection pools. (medium confidence)
Call client.close when finished, or construct the client with a Ruby block so it closes automatically when the block finishes. (low confidence)

Coinbase reported in its June 18, 2020 case study that per-process Ruby pools and overlapping blue-green deployments multiplied MongoDB connections. It introduced a connection proxy after finding many connections mostly unused; this is historical workload evidence, not a general requirement to deploy a proxy. (low confidence)
A `CodecRegistry` is immutable. Compose custom codecs or providers with the default registry, placing custom codecs first when overriding defaults. (low confidence)

Use `DB::table()` to select a MongoDB collection, chain constraints, and finish with `get()` or `first()`. Select a named MongoDB connection with `DB::connection()` when MongoDB is not the default connection. (low confidence)

Configure attribute conversions with `$casts`; the documented model example casts a BSON date field to Laravel `datetime`. Allow-list mass-assignable fields with `$fillable`, or exclude fields with `$guarded`. (low confidence)
Install the library with composer require mongodb/mongodb and separately install and enable the mongodb extension; the library requires that extension. (high confidence)
Use insert_one for a single document and insert_many for a list of documents. (low confidence)
Use delete_one to remove the first matching document and delete_many to remove all matching documents; both accept a query filter. (medium confidence)

Use insert_one for a single document and insert_many for a list of documents. If the application does not supply _id, the driver can generate unique BSON::ObjectId values; duplicate _id values violate the unique index. (low confidence)

Use update_one for the first matching document and update_many for all matches, supplying a query filter and an update document such as a $set operation. Set upsert: true to insert when no document matches. (low confidence)

Issue #2720 reports that Laravel MongoDB 4.1 raised `Transaction already in progress` when `firstOrCreate()` attempted creation inside an existing transaction. A maintainer attributed the error to an attempted nested transaction and described replacing that implementation with an atomic operation. This is historical issue evidence, not verification of current installed behavior. (low confidence)

Composer platform requirements describe the PHP environment and its extensions as virtual packages. Requiring a platform package installs no code; it cannot substitute for installing the native mongodb extension required by the PHP library. (high confidence)

Ordered bulk writes stop after a write-operation failure. With ordered: false, the driver attempts all specified operations and reports write errors after those attempts; execution order is not guaranteed. (medium confidence)
Iterate query results with each to consume a cursor that holds a subset of results in memory; chained limit and sort options refine the query results. (low confidence)

Update results distinguish matched_count from modified_count: an identical document is excluded from modified_count. Check acknowledged? before reading other result methods; an unacknowledged result cannot provide those values. (low confidence)

Collection#bulk_write accepts a list of operation hashes, including insert_one, update_one, update_many, replace_one, delete_one and delete_many. Ordered execution stops after a write error; ordered: false attempts the remaining operations without guaranteeing execution order. (low confidence)

A pool limit is not a deployment-wide connection limit: the Ruby pool guide also describes monitoring connections outside the application pool, and Coinbase documented separate pools for Ruby processes, shared by their threads. (medium confidence)

Scala migration guidance says the Scala 3 compiler cannot expand Scala 2.13 macros. Using `-Xignore-scala2-macros` permits type checking but macro calls throw at runtime; use a library version published for Scala 3. (low confidence)

Set query-level options through `options()`. MongoDB recommends using the dedicated query-builder methods for result modifiers such as skip, sort and limit rather than passing these modifiers as options. (low confidence)

Callbacks customize model lifecycle events and can be implemented on top-level and embedded documents. The docs recommend testing callback chains and using callbacks for cross-cutting concerns rather than core domain logic. (low confidence)

The server-selection guide describes filtering read candidates by read preference, applying the localThresholdMS latency window, and selecting randomly among remaining candidates. For writes it starts with writable servers rather than read-preference matches. (low confidence)

The pool guide conflicts with the connection-options reference and client source on max_idle_time units: its detailed example calls 10000 milliseconds ten seconds, whereas the reference maps max_idle_time: 10 to maxIdleTimeMS=10000 and the client source documents seconds. Treat the pool-guide example as conflicting documentation rather than a safe Ruby configuration to copy. (low confidence)
Laravel MongoDB extends Laravel’s Eloquent and query-builder APIs to operate on MongoDB data. (high confidence)
Define a MongoDB Eloquent model by extending `MongoDB\Laravel\Eloquent\Model`. (high confidence)
Models use the snake-case plural class name as the default collection; override `$table` to choose another collection. (low confidence)

A MongoDB Eloquent model can use the `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes` trait: deleting marks the document with `deleted_at`, and normal retrieval automatically excludes deleted documents. (high confidence)
The query-builder documentation says results are `stdClass` objects starting in Laravel MongoDB v5.0. (low confidence)

The integration exposes MongoDB `_id` through the `id` alias; query-builder find results present `_id` as `id`, so separate fields with both names are incompatible with that conversion. (high confidence)

Laravel MongoDB supports explicit transaction control with `DB::beginTransaction()`, `DB::commit()`, and `DB::rollback()` before commit. Rollback reverts writes performed in the transaction. (medium confidence)

Standalone MongoDB deployments do not support these transactions. The Laravel MongoDB transaction guide prescribes a replica set or sharded cluster, rejects nested transactions with a `RuntimeException`, and disallows parallel operations inside a single transaction. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The transaction guide states that Laravel MongoDB does not support `Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\DatabaseTransactions` or `Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase`; it suggests `Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\DatabaseMigrations` to reset the database after each test. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Issue #2720 reported `firstOrCreate()` failing inside a transaction on Laravel MongoDB 4.1 with “Transaction already in progress”; the 4.2 release announcement says the issue was fixed by implementing `Model::createOrFirst()` with atomic `findOneAndUpdate`. (high confidence)
Laravel MongoDB provides MongoDB-backed Eloquent models and a fluent query builder; Laravel documents the integration as the mongodb/laravel-mongodb package maintained by MongoDB. (medium confidence)

Define a MongoDB Eloquent model by extending `MongoDB\Laravel\Eloquent\Model`. The default collection name is the snake case plural of the model class name; override `$table` to choose another collection. (low confidence)

MongoDB stores the primary key in `_id`; the Laravel integration exposes it as `$id` on a model and translates query-builder `id` references to `_id`. The model can customize the identifier type with `$keyType`. (low confidence)
The query builder supports filtering nested fields with dotted paths, sorting with `orderBy()`, and skipping results with `skip()`; `whereRaw()` accepts MongoDB Query API filters. (low confidence)

A persistent Mongoid model includes `Mongoid::Document`; typed fields can be declared with `field :name, type: String`. Instances can be stored in a collection or embedded in other documents. (low confidence)

Embedded associations use `embeds_one` or `embeds_many` on the parent and `embedded_in` on the child. The child is stored inside the parent; multiple children are stored as an array field. (high confidence)
Referenced associations support `has_one`, `has_many`, `belongs_to`, and `has_and_belongs_to_many`. By default, `belongs_to` stores the parent’s `_id` in the child document. (low confidence)

Association callbacks `before_add`, `after_add`, `before_remove`, and `after_remove` apply to `embeds_many`, `has_many`, and `has_and_belongs_to_many`. Register them as association options and pass the added or removed document to the callback. (low confidence)

Deletion paths have different callback semantics: document `delete` skips callbacks while `destroy` runs them; for embedded associations, `clear` and `delete_all` skip destroy callbacks while `destroy_all` runs them. (medium confidence)
Mongoid query methods return chainable, lazily evaluated `Mongoid::Criteria` objects. Iterating results executes the query; chaining query methods merges filter criteria. (low confidence)

Embedded matching filters associations already loaded in the application without querying the server. Its supported operators are narrower than server queries: text, geospatial, JavaScript execution, `$expr`, and `$jsonSchema` are not implemented. (low confidence)

A historical embedded-assignment performance investigation attributed increasing Ruby-side work to `object_already_related?`; Alex Bevilacqua profiled the issue without a database connection. This supports profiling association construction separately from database operations, not an unconditional claim that current releases retain the defect. (medium confidence)
A persistent Mongoid model includes `Mongoid::Document`; model instances can live in a collection or be embedded, and saving converts them to BSON. (low confidence)

Referenced associations support `has_one`, `has_many`, `belongs_to`, and `has_and_belongs_to_many`. By default a belongs-to child stores the parent identifier; many-to-many associations store arrays of associated identifiers on both sides unless the inverse is disabled. (low confidence)

Query filters support Ruby field hashes, Query API operator hashes, and symbol operators. For fields declared in the model, Mongoid coerces filter values to the field type; `Mongoid::RawValue` bypasses that coercion. (low confidence)

`elem_match` requires at least one array element to satisfy all supplied conditions and supports embedded associations. It does not join referenced associations; cross-collection querying needs an aggregation pipeline or separate queries. (high confidence)

Mongoid provides document lifecycle callbacks for top-level and embedded models. Association callbacks `before_add`, `after_add`, `before_remove`, and `after_remove` are configured on `embeds_many`, `has_many`, or `has_and_belongs_to_many` and receive the affected document. (low confidence)

The extension supplies the low-level connection management, BSON encoding/decoding, command/query/write execution, and cursor functionality. It connects PHP to libmongoc, libbson, and libmongocrypt. (high confidence)

The extension can be used directly without the PHP library. The PHP manual and library maintainers recommend the library or another high-level abstraction for most application development. (high confidence)
The legacy mongo extension has a different API from the newer mongodb extension and PHP library; migrating existing legacy applications requires API adaptation. (high confidence)

A September 2026 Herd issue reports a library upgrade blocked by the bundled extension: the reporter says mongodb/mongodb 2.4.1 requires ext-mongodb ^2.4 while Herd supplies 2.3.3. This is a report about that environment, not a universal package compatibility statement. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-09)
After installing the library, load Composer's vendor/autoload.php in the application so Composer-installed classes are available. (high confidence)

Collection#find accepts a query filter and returns a Mongo::Collection::View; execution is deferred until results are requested with first or each. Chain first to retrieve one matching document. (low confidence)
update_one changes the first matching document; update_many changes all matching documents. Both take a query filter and an update document. (low confidence)
bulk_write accepts a list of operation hashes covering insert_one, update_one, update_many, replace_one, delete_one and delete_many. (medium confidence)
Each Mongo::Client has a connection pool for each server in the topology. Connections are reused, and without a configured min_pool_size, pools open connections on demand. (low confidence)
max_pool_size limits concurrent pooled connections per server, while max_connecting limits concurrent connection establishment per pool; these are different capacity controls. (medium confidence)
The connection-options reference distinguishes server_selection_timeout, which bounds waiting for server selection, from connection-pool capacity settings. (low confidence)

The shared connection-pooling specification requires thread-safe pool behavior but explicitly declares connections and pools not fork-safe; its reset-after-fork procedure clears pools and closes connections in the child. This is a specification requirement, not verification of a particular Ruby release’s fork hooks. (low confidence)

Each Mongo::Client maintains a pool per topology server. Pool capacity and concurrent connection creation are separate controls: max_pool_size limits pool size and max_connecting limits parallel connection establishment. (medium confidence)

The Ruby connection-options reference expresses connect_timeout and server_selection_timeout in seconds, while the corresponding URI options are connectTimeoutMS and serverSelectionTimeoutMS in milliseconds. The reference describes timeout_ms as an operation timeout in milliseconds. (medium confidence)
The Scala driver builds on the MongoDB Java Reactive Streams driver; its `Observable` extends `Publisher` and adds convenience methods for processing operation results. (low confidence)

Calling `subscribe()` with an `Observer` requests operation results; `FindObservable[T]`, `DistinctObservable[T]`, and `AggregateObservable[T]` also support operation-specific configuration before subscription. (low confidence)
An `Observer` receives results through `onNext`, terminal failures through `onError`, and completion through `onComplete`; subscription overloads also accept lambda callbacks. (medium confidence)

Calling `toFuture()` implicitly subscribes and collects emitted items; for a large document result set this can consume significant memory, so the guide recommends callbacks or lambdas. (low confidence)
The historical Scala driver 2.1 contract allows multiple subscriptions to an `Observable`, with each subscription potentially repeating side effects such as queries or inserts. (low confidence)
The custom case-class example obtains field codecs from a `CodecRegistry` and attaches the composed registry to a typed collection using `withCodecRegistry()`. (low confidence)
